content.title: “They Have Come to Take Me; I Am Leaving…”—A 26-Year-Old’s Final Farewell
content.subtitle: Has Sabbir Bhai’s departure not lifted the veil from our eyes?
content.body:
He was only twenty-six. Six feet two inches tall, with a strong build and eyes full of dreams. After completing his Civil Engineering degree from the University of Asia Pacific, he had just begun his professional life. He spent his days working as a Site Engineer at a private construction firm. His father was retired from the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB). The eldest of three siblings, he was the family’s greatest source of support. They lived in Basila, Dhaka, while their roots were in a peaceful village in Joypurhat.

Quiet, humble, and gentle by nature, he would often say during breaks from work, “I don’t enjoy this job anymore. Give me a good business idea so I can start something of my own.” Before his dreams could take flight, a difficult test suddenly entered his life.

The Silent Hospital Corridor and His Final Words

It was October 2, 2026. Blood cancer, followed by the devastating blow of dengue. After a prolonged illness, his strength was gradually fading. A heavy silence hung outside the ICU of a specialized hospital near Dhaka PG Hospital.

As his condition deteriorated rapidly, the doctors said he needed to be placed on life support. His lifeless body lay on a hospital trolley, yet the final light of consciousness was still flickering. Just before being taken for life support, he looked toward his mother and said in a calm voice:

“Everyone is praying for me… You pray for me too. They have come to take me. I am leaving.”

A few moments later, his heartbeat stopped. The light of a vibrant twenty-six-year-old life was extinguished.

Sabbir Bhai—A Grief Very Close to Us

This is not the story of some distant stranger. Sabbir Ahmed (Sifat) Bhai was the cousin of our colleague, Abid Mehedi Bhai. When we heard these moments through Abid Bhai’s tearful account, our hearts became heavy in an instant.

Before our eyes appeared the image of a young man leaving behind immense potential, countless dreams, and unfinished stories before departing for the Hereafter.

How Long Will We Remain Careless in the Illusion of Youth?

We often think of youth as the time to build a career, chase colorful dreams, and enjoy life to the fullest. Somewhere in our minds, we may assume that worship and repentance can wait until old age—that when our hair turns gray and our skin begins to wrinkle, we will settle down on the prayer mat.

But has Sabbir Bhai’s sudden departure not lifted the veil from our eyes? Does death wait for us to build our careers? Does the Angel of Death ever send a notice based on our age?

Endless Time—or Merely a Mirage?

How little we understand the Prophet ﷺ’s reminder to value our youth before it passes away. That six-foot-two-inch body now lies silently beneath the soil of the grave. Yet we continue to imagine that we have endless time to return to our Lord.

In this quiet moment, close your eyes and ask yourself: If my call comes today, what will I take with me when I stand before my Lord?

Our worldly careers and countless plans may remain behind. What will accompany us are only the good deeds we performed for Allah’s pleasure and the ongoing charity we left behind. Are we ready? Are we preparing for that eternal journey?
